headline: Tōtoi is from Old Japanese, first attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE, and is possibly derived from 太い (futoi, “fat”).

sources.quote: ⟨taputo₁ki⟩ → */taɸutokʲi/ → /toːtoi/

From Old Japanese. First attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE. From Early Middle Japanese adjective 尊(とうと)し (tōtoshi), with the 終(しゅう)止(し)形(けい) (shūshikei, “predicative form”) ending in し (shi) first replaced with the 連(れん)体(たい)形(けい) (rentaikei, “attributive form”) ending in き (ki), and then with the medial /-k-/ falling out to result in an ending of い (i).
Possibly derived from 太い (futoi, “fat”).

headline: Wakusei is a calque of Dutch dwaalster (“wander star”), 惑 (waku, “to move about confusedly, to wander”) plus 星 (sei, “star”), coined in 1792 by Motoki Yoshinaga.

morphemes.meaning: to move about confusedly, to wander

sources.quote: Wasei kango: Calque of Dutch dwaalster (literally “wander star”), composed as a compound of 惑 (waku, “to move about confusedly, to wander”) + 星 (sei, “star”). Probably related to 熒惑 (MC hweng hwok).

Coined in 1792 by Dutch-Japanese translator Motoki Yoshinaga in his 太陽窮理了解説 (Taiyō Kyūri Ryōkai Setsu, “Theory of Understanding on the Natural Study of the Sun”), a translation of Copernicus's De revolutionibus orbium coelestium and its heliocentric model.
Also cited in the 1805 work 和蘭通舶 (Oranda Tsūhaku, “Holland Liner”) by Shiba Kōkan.

headline: Seigi is from Middle Chinese 正義, and in the Meiji era it was repurposed to translate Western concepts of “justice”.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 正義 (MC tsyeng|tsyengH ngjeH). Originally referred to the “correct meaning” or “orthodox interpretation” of classical Chinese texts (first attested in Japanese in the Kirei Mondō (貴嶺問答), 1185–1190), as well as “proper righteousness” (attested in the Gukanshō (愚管抄), 1220).
During the Meiji era, the term was repurposed to translate Western legal and philosophical concepts of “justice” (such as English justice, French justice, or German Gerechtigkeit).
